summary:
One night, during a power cut, Aiza Malik discovers NASA's list of human-made objects left on the Moon. It has not been updated since 2012. Aiza promises that if nobody else will, she will keep the list alive.
Seven years later, she lands on the Moon, where her AI assistant SAFAR helps her. She finds old footprints, a laser reflector that still works, rovers, the Fallen Astronaut, a family photograph and 96 bags of waste. She realises that not everything is rubbish. Some things were left for work, and some for the heart.
Dr. Nadia Rizvi then tells her about the debris on Mars. There, wind moves the debris around, and it could contaminate samples stored in sealed tubes. Mars has never had a human visitor, so every piece was left by machines.
Aiza understands that the same act, leaving something behind, is heritage on the Moon but a hazard on Mars. She decides to create a "living register" in which every mission, before launch, records what it carries, what it will leave and what it will bring home.
In the end, she carries her own rubbish back to the lander. Her message: leave footprints, and take everything else home.
details:
Project Details: "The Keepers of the Quiet"

Team: Team Algorix

Type: Space-themed story for the NASA story writing competition

1. Overview

The story follows Aiza Malik, a university student who finds NASA's list of human-made objects on the Moon. The list has not been updated since 2012. She promises to keep it alive. Seven years later she lands on the Moon, learns about the debris on Mars, and creates a "living register" that records what every space mission carries, leaves and brings home.

2. Background and Inspiration

NASA keeps a catalogue of human-made material left on the Moon, last updated in 2012.

Many objects there are not just equipment, including a memorial figure, a family photograph and bags of waste.

Researchers at West Virginia University estimated in 2022 that about 7,000 kg of human-made debris lies on Mars. This is an estimate, not an official NASA figure.

The project asks a simple question: when humans leave things on other worlds, who remembers them and who looks after them?

3. Aims

Tell an engaging story that makes real space facts easy to understand.

Show that objects left in space can be heritage, memory or hazard, depending on the place.

Encourage responsible, shared care of other worlds.

Reach two audiences, with the complete story in English and in Roman Urdu.

4. Main Ideas

The living register: Instead of a finished list, a record that keeps growing. Before every launch, each mission writes down what it carries, what it will leave and what it will bring home.

Three new catalogue columns: Why was it left? What does it mean today? Who will look after it?

Heritage versus hazard: The same act, leaving something behind, is heritage on the Moon (nothing moves) but a hazard on Mars (wind moves debris and could contaminate sealed samples).

Tools versus memories: Some things were left for work, and some for the heart.

Choosing, not littering: The Apollo crews made choices that were right for their time. Now the choice belongs to us.

Shared responsibility: A register needs many countries to agree, so Aiza starts with one entry.

5. Characters

Aiza Malik: A student who grows into a lunar survey scientist. She drives the idea.

SAFAR: Her AI survey assistant. It measures, scans and records, and helps her see both sides.

Dr. Nadia Rizvi: A mission planner who brings the Mars problem to Aiza.

6. Story Structure

The Night the Lights Went Out: Aiza finds the 2012 list and makes her promise.

A Quiet Landing: On the Moon, old footprints and a working mirror panel show that these objects are still alive in meaning.

The Small Things: Three rovers, a hand-cart, golf balls, the Fallen Astronaut, a family photo and 96 waste bags.

The Red Neighbour: Mars debris comes in three kinds: discarded hardware, silent machines and crashed craft.

Two Meanings: Aiza adds the three columns and decides to create the living register.

The Last Line: She writes a promise as her newest entry, carries her own rubbish home, and answers her old sentence with "Someone did."

7. Themes and Message

Memory, responsibility, care for shared spaces, and the courage to start something small.

Core message: Leave footprints, and take everything else home.

8. Why This Project Stands Out

It combines real facts with an original idea, the living register.

It is told through a relatable student character.

It is complete in English with a ready presentation.
